page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 series, built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor delivering 32 vCPUs mapped across 16 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU runs at 3.525 GHz and includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, though AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Memory performance shows strong efficiency, registering a PassMark memory score in the upper quartile alongside 83.57 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 47.79 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth on 256 MB blocks. Bundled ephemeral storage consists of a 275 GB local solid-state drive, suitable for temporary caches, scratch space, and swap files. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs provisioned on this instance.

Benchmark results place the D32as_v4 primarily in the middle 50 percent tier for multi-core throughput, recording a PassMark CPU score of 39340.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14416.0. Single-core stress-ng testing shows upper-quartile behavior at 2707.6, while software compilation via Clang achieves 23764.0 points. In caching tests, the configuration handled 31.62 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 25.09 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. Natural language inference on small models reaches 330.2 tokens per second for text generation, though large 70-billion-parameter prompt processing drops to the bottom 25 percent due to the absence of dedicated tensor hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32as_v4 offers strong compute density and memory allocations relative to its standard tier without incurring accelerator overheads. The balanced architecture suits multi-tier enterprise web serving, backend relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build nodes, and general business applications requiring sustained multi-threaded CPU performance.
